description.p: ObserverLauncher is a desktop app for hosting Minecraft servers on your own computer, made for both beginners and power users. Pick a folder, choose a server type, and it downloads, starts and manages everything for you.
Features:

ul.li: Guided setup for Vanilla, Paper, Purpur, Fabric, Forge and NeoForge servers
Live console, player list, performance charts and a world map from your save
Install plugins, mods and datapacks from the built-in Marketplace
Scheduled backups, crash auto-restart and a share-to-internet tunnel
Runs fully offline; optional local AI/MCP integration

The World Map tab rendered from a world save

description.p: Pre-start conflict scanner detects duplicates, wrong loaders, missing dependencies and incompatible mods directly in the Content tab. Updates can be applied in bulk with automatic file backups, immediate undo toast actions, manual rollback, and an automatic crash-recovery rollback guard. Loose jar files copied into the server folder now display their internal versions.

Marketplace builds on Hangar now honour the version you pick and match your Minecraft release, and proxy plugins for Velocity can be installed. Console player links work when the name uses different casing or lives in the whitelist. The 3D player viewer cleans up its mouse listeners and graphic resources when closed. Saving game rules or datapack order no longer leaves endless backup files behind, and the server message field gains quick colour buttons.

Bug fixes and a few honest labels. The server message preview now shows the colours the player will actually see. Spigot plugins show the author's name in the install window. Installing a CurseForge modpack no longer leaves half the pack behind when a file fails to download.

Bedrock players can join a Java server without editing config files by hand: the app repairs a Geyser config in one click and opens a second tunnel for the Bedrock side. Metrics history now reaches back a month. The player inspector draws a rotatable 3D model with the player's armor and reads item icons from the server's own mod jars, and skins come from SkinsRestorer on offline-mode servers. Also adds Discord notifications, a Prometheus endpoint, multi-server controls and a hardening pass.
The Playit tunnel address is now detected automatically from the agent log instead of being copied by hand, and the app surfaces a Bedrock crossplay panel when GeyserMC is installed.

The in-client MCP Apps dashboard now covers more tools: the server health diagnosis and the full doctor report render a colour-coded check list, and the player list renders grouped player chips. The metrics charts from 5.5.0 are unchanged.

The MCP server now advertises an in-client dashboard for the metrics tool: a supporting AI client such as Claude Desktop draws line charts for TPS, MSPT, CPU, RAM and players right beside the result. Clients that do not support MCP Apps still get the same data as text.
The Performance tab keeps a full day of history and now saves it to disk, so the 24h chart is still there after you restart the app.

Fix: changing the interface language now follows the Apply button (like the other settings) instead of switching instantly, and a fresh install with no server folder can still change it. Also translated the last remaining English strings (onboarding, the New Server wizard and the server properties editor) into all seven languages.

Marketplace fixes: the compatibility panel now shows your exact server software (Leaf, Purpur, Folia - not just "Paper"), and CurseForge projects list their dependencies. The Performance tab gains 1h and 6h chart ranges. The Windows installer now explains the SmartScreen warning.
Fix: the LAN address the launcher shares for friends to join could be a virtual network adapter (VPN, Docker, virtual machine) that is unreachable. The real WiFi/Ethernet address is now preferred.
A new Beginner mode shows only the essentials (Overview, Console, Players, Settings) with a one-click way to reveal every tool, plus a prominent "share this address" card when the server is running.
An AI client can now create a new server (it opens a folder picker for you) and is told what Java a server needs; a wedged app can no longer hang the AI. Also adds an early MCP Apps preview.

A major MCP upgrade: the AI integration now exposes tool annotations, workflow prompts, output schemas and dynamic resource templates, so an AI client can auto-approve safe reads and follow ready-made workflows.
Give each server its own colour and generated avatar, and fix the New Server wizard's version and Java handling for Forge, NeoForge, Paper, Purpur, Leaf and Velocity.
Remote access now includes a small web dashboard you can open in a browser (status, console, players), plus token hardening and a stability fix.
Security: remote-access settings (bind, allowed IPs, read-only, port) now apply immediately when you Save; add token reveal and rotation.
Security and fixes: MCP output hygiene (hide player IPs and config secrets from AI clients), World Map fixes.
Housekeeping release: removed unused translation strings and added a test that keeps them out.
